text:
marta: heads up — getting a flood of DCGM alerts from us-west-2 this morning, mostly ECC and a handful of Xid on gpunode-4a and gpunode-4b. started right after last kernel pkg push.

alex: +1 saw ~40 alerts in 6m, many from the same physical card. PD incident already created (pd-5432). wondering if we should suppress noise vs trigger full oncall.

maria: i think we should classify by error type: corrected ECC -> warning; uncorrected ECC or repeated Xid -> page. we also need per-card aggregation so we dont get 40 pages for 1 flaky card.

lee: agreed. propose a short-lived suppression for corrected-ecc spikes and a recording rule to aggregate counts by gpu_card and node. then alert on rate and unique_card_count. sample recording rule: 
```
- record: gpu:ecc_corrected:rate5m
  expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_single_bit_corrected_total[5m])
```
alert rule example: 
```
- alert: MultipleCorrectedECCs
  expr: sum by (node) (gpu:ecc_corrected:rate5m) > 10
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    summary: 'node {{ $labels.node }} high corrected ECC rate'
    runbook: 'link to quick triage playbook'
```

marta: nice. also add a finger-print label with gpu_slot so we can group. we should annotate with "suppressable:true" when it looks like post-kernel noise so ops can flip a temporary silence.

oncall-bot: pagerduty incident pd-5432 triggered (sev: page). linked alert: MultipleUncorrectedECCs node=gpunode-4a

alex: what about noisy Xid 61s? those often clear on reboot. for node drains we lose capacity — that matters for throughput today. maybe prefer remote reboot then drain if it recurs.

maria: agree. add escalation window: if same card fires >3 uncorrected/Xid in 1h -> auto drain annotation. else try soft-reboot with monitoring 15m. also track replacement candidates via tag replacement: candidate=true.

lee: operational checklist snippet (to paste in runbook): 
1) check ec2 instance console for ECC phys errors
2) try soft reboot: `sudo systemctl restart dcgm-exporter` then `sudo reboot` if metrics persist
3) if >3 uncorrected errors or Xid 61s in 1h -> cordon+drain node, schedule node replacement
4) annotate alert with hardware-ticket and replacement tag

marta: i will open a short-lived alert-suppression change in monitoring (5m window to test) and push recording/alert rules to staging. can someone run canary against us-west test pool?

alex: i'll run canary against the us-west test pool in 15m and report back. tagging @maria for rule review.

maria: will review now. also, note cost tradeoff: aggressive auto-drain increases spot eviction / replacement cost and temporarily reduces capacity. documented in the runbook section 'cost impacts'.

oncall-bot: deploy-bot started deploy pipeline #ci-1298 for prometheus-rules/staging

deploy-bot: CI passed, staging rules applied to prometheus-staging (ruleset id rs-77).

alex: staging looks quiet after suppression + new recording rules enabled. will monitor 30m then flip to prod if stable.

marta: thanks team. after prod flip, we should add an alert annotation linking to the new severity mapping and the hardware replacement queue. closing the loop here. :thumbsup:
